Independent proof reconstruction via the exact rectangular-block factorial moment, color-concentration tail and signature-fibre comparison
correctness.rationale: Conditioning on colors makes the q² ordered edge blocks independent. The zero-row and zero-column counts in C_a×C_b are X⁺_{ab} and X⁻_{ba}. Their conditional mixed factorial moment of orders r,s is (N_a)_r(N_b)_s(1−p_n)^(rN_b+sN_a−rs): exactly rs entries are selected both ways, also in diagonal blocks because loops are included. Uniformly for |N_c−n/q|≤n^(2/3), this tends to λ^(r+s); the complementary probability is exp(−Ω(n^(1/3))) and fixed factorial moments there are bounded by fixed powers of n. This proves the joint moment convergence to independent moment-determinate Poisson coordinates. Two different hole constraints at one vertex share at most a loop, so a union bound gives o(1) probability of any multiple-hole vertex. The tight total hole count and linearly large color classes give a hole-free representative of each color with high probability. The actual modal generator signature then has one default fibre per color and one additional fibre for each positive hole count. This yields the binomial excess law, and |B_1| converges in distribution to 2^(q+J), rather than having an exact finite-n binomial formula. With a hole-free representative in each color, closure of B_0 under the two union-preserving modalities is equivalent to no holes, giving exp(−2q e^(−t)). When |t_n|=o(log n), the total hole expectation is asymptotic to 2q e^(−t_n). It vanishes on the upper side. On the lower side an outgoing block count alone is conditionally binomial with diverging mean, while the total remains o_p(n), so at least one class splits with high probability. These claims concern the high-density window, not global monotonicity.
residual_risks: No separate finite replay was required for the asymptotic proof. The law for full closure is only a saturation probability; it does not give the structure or distribution of B_∞ conditional on nonsaturation.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: With m=floor(n/q), the shift for the square array is c=t+log q+o(1). Missing or extra rows and columns against a common square coupling are O(n^(2/3)) on the color event. The probability that one is isolated is collectively O(n^(−1/3)); changing an isolated row or column's status via those added entries costs O(n^(−1/3) log n) in expectation. Thus the known pair law transfers; q² edge-disjoint blocks extend it to the joint vector. This identifies probabilistic coverage even without identical parameters.

originality.rationale: The square Bernoulli zero-row/zero-column joint Poisson law is already explicit in Resultary 3c40796d6471. Conditioning on colors, perturbing the dimensions negligibly from a square, and taking independent blocks give the probabilistic vector by a direct known-law reduction, so it is not credited as a standalone novelty. The supported distinct claim is the directed two-way tense-algebra application: the all-hole-type signature-fibre mechanism, exact critical first-step atom distribution, and resulting full-saturation window for fixed color palettes. The closest inspected modal results have different underlying worlds and different type-count mechanisms or limits.
residual_risks: Unread precise passages in Halpern–Kapron remain an adjacent literature risk; no whole-paper claim is made. Equivalent sparse logical extension-axiom or random-algebra formulations may be unindexed. The square isolation law is verified covered regardless of those gaps.

value.rationale: For a fixed palette, the law quantifies how much one application of the two tense operations enlarges the generated Boolean algebra and identifies the threshold for no enlargement at any depth. The nondegenerate explicit atom law uses the number of realized defect types rather than the number of defective vertices. The contrast is useful in the random algebra setting; multiplication of known block Poisson laws alone would not justify a value pass.
residual_risks: Fixed q, independent ordered edges with loops, and the high-density window only. Does not characterize the growth of deeper refinement upon nonsaturation.
